target_customer: Companies with hybrid offices that need desk, room and visitor management
problem: Hybrid teams cannot easily find the best time and space to collaborate. Zynq lets employees book desks and rooms, host guests, and gives managers space analytics.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with pricing tiers

founders.name: Zerzar Bukhari
founders.background_notes: From the YC page: product manager at Google and Microsoft, founder of Marble and Cartesia.

founders.name: David Cottrell
founders.background_notes: YC page: G Suite software engineer at Google and first engineer at Spacebar. CTO role from Crunchbase via search summary.

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, calendar integrations and analytics are standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Many desk booking vendors existed and integrations with calendars and access systems are copyable; stickiness comes from enterprise integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it in sources. Infigos is reported by one aggregator to have acquired it in May 2026.

market_need_then: Hybrid work rose sharply from 2020, and the YC description positions the product for hybrid workplaces; no spend figures found.

branding.domain_note: Uses zynq.io, not the .com; ZYNQ is also a registered trademark of Xilinx (filed 2010) for FPGA chips.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product led; tagline about organizing people, space and time

brand_strength.rationale: Search results for the name are dominated by Xilinx Zynq chips, and no brand coverage for the workplace product was found.

outcome_analysis: Zynq built a hybrid office management product in a crowded desk booking category and raised little money that sources confirm. Its exit is reported only by an aggregator and the YC page, which say an acquisition by Infigos was announced in May 2026, long after its 2020 batch, which suggests a slow outcome rather than a rapid venture win. Search was also hampered by the name overlapping the Xilinx Zynq chip trademark, though no source shows lost customers from it.
notes: Seedtable exit page returned 403 when fetched; the Infigos acquisition and May 2026 date come from a search summary of Seedtable and the YC status, and no primary announcement was found, so unverified. Seed of 150 thousand dollars from Y Combinator in March 2020 is a single CB Insights figure, not recorded as a round. Competitor list empty because comparison pages found are 2025 to 2026 and undated for 2020. brand_confusion failure factor is speculative and supported only by the trademark overlap.
